title: Two-dimensional sandpile prediction in NC
formal: Is the language \(\mathrm{SP}_2\) defined below in logspace-uniform \(\mathrm{NC}\)? An instance explicitly supplies a finite stable rectangular array of sand grains and cells \(p,q\) inside that rectangle. Extend the array by zero to all of \(\mathbb Z^2\), add one grain at \(p\), and accept exactly when \(q\) eventually topples under the simultaneous four-neighbor rule. The question concerns one uniform circuit family with polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth for all input lengths.
definitions:
Let \(W,H\ge1\), let \(B=\{0,\ldots,W-1\}\times\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\), let \(c:B\to\{0,1,2,3\}\), and let \(p=(p_x,p_y),q=(q_x,q_y)\in B\). Define \(\bar c(v)=c(v)\) on \(B\) and \(\bar c(v)=0\) elsewhere in \(\mathbb Z^2\). Set \(c_0(v)=\bar c(v)+\mathbf1_{\{v=p\}}\). With
\[
E=\{(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)\},
\]
define, for every integer \(t\ge0\) and every \(v\in\mathbb Z^2\),
\[
c_{t+1}(v)=c_t(v)-4\mathbf1_{\{c_t(v)\ge4\}}+
\sum_{e\in E}\mathbf1_{\{c_t(v-e)\ge4\}}.
\]
Here \(\mathbf1_A\) is \(1\) when assertion \(A\) holds and \(0\) otherwise. Every unstable cell topples once per simultaneous round; its threshold and the number of grains sent to each neighbor are fixed. The required output is \(1\) exactly when \(\exists t\ge0:\ c_t(q)\ge4\). All cells outside the supplied rectangle participate in the same dynamics. There is no absorbing boundary, periodic identification, missing neighbor or cell-dependent weight.

For a nonnegative integer \(z\), let \(s(z)\) be its ordinary binary expansion without leading zeros, using \(s(0)=0\), and let \(b(z)=|s(z)|\). Encode \(z\) as \(1^{b(z)}0s(z)\). A valid binary input is the concatenation of these codes for \(W,H,p_x,p_y,q_x,q_y\), followed by exactly \(2WH\) bits encoding the entries of \(c\): list rows in increasing \(y\), and within each row increasing \(x\), using \(00,01,10,11\) for \(0,1,2,3\). Dimensions must be positive and the encoded coordinates must belong to \(B\). Strings not meeting these conditions are rejected. Let \(N\) be the complete binary string length, including all array entries. Extra zero rows or columns are permitted, but their entries still count; this is not a sparse or succinct configuration encoding.

Membership in logspace-uniform \(\mathrm{NC}\) means that there exist fixed integers \(a,k\ge1\), a fixed real \(K\ge1\), and a deterministic finite Turing-machine program generating a Boolean circuit \(C_N\) from the unary input \(1^N\), for every \(N\ge0\). It must halt, use at most \(K\log_2(N+2)\) work-tape cells, and write an explicit gate-and-wire description to a write-only output tape. Its input tape is read-only. The circuit has \(N\) input bits and one output, uses AND and OR gates of fan-in two, NOT gates of fan-in one and constants \(0,1\), has at most \(K(N+2)^a\) gates and depth at most \(K(\log_2(N+2))^k\), and decides \(\mathrm{SP}_2\) exactly on all length-\(N\) strings. Gate descriptions use binary indices in topological order and specify the output gate. There is no advice or oracle. The constants, circuit generator and gate basis are independent of the instance. Randomized error is not allowed; no time \(t\) is supplied as part of the instance.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of membership of this language in the specified uniform circuit class, or a complete Lean proof that no such circuit family and generator exist. Polynomial sequential simulation alone is insufficient. A proof of P-completeness under logspace reductions would imply nonmembership only with the additional assumption that P differs from NC; it is not an unconditional negative answer.
why: One extra grain can trigger a long deterministic cascade. Whether its eventual effect can always be computed in polylogarithmic parallel time is a canonical test of how much sequential dependence a simple physical process can express.

importance.reason: A canonical unresolved parallel-complexity question for a simple two-dimensional dynamical system, connecting computational prediction with statistical physics.

context_blocks.text: The 2025 source defines eventual prediction from a finite stable configuration plus one grain on the infinite lattice. This card retains that decision question for the ordinary four-neighbor rule, with an explicit array encoding, and asks for its NC-membership branch. It does not ask for an entire final configuration or a toppling at a supplied time.

Moore and Nilsson establish \(\mathrm{NC}^3\) prediction in one dimension and P-completeness in dimensions at least three, in their finite-lattice formulation. Their two-dimensional discussion remains a foundational motivation; the direct definition used here comes from the 2025 infinite-lattice source.

The June 2026 paper continues to describe ordinary planar prediction as unsettled while studying weighted and nonuniform variants. Its formal finite-grid model includes a sink at the boundary. That convention is distinguished from the zero-extended infinite lattice fixed here.
The March 2026 fungal-automaton result concerns alternating horizontal and vertical update rules. It does not provide a classification of the simultaneous four-neighbor dynamics in this card.

progress.text: The classical work separates one-dimensional and higher-dimensional prediction, leaving the two-dimensional case unresolved.
The primary eventual-prediction definition is explicitly distinguished from the timed problem; the von Neumann-neighborhood case remains open in that source.
The revised fungal-automaton preprint classifies a different family of update schemes.
The weighted and nonuniform crossing paper retains the unresolved standard planar question and states its distinct finite-grid boundary convention.
Rechecked source models, repaired the update formula, fixed the language encoding and added a complete Lean criterion.

category_assignment.reason: The decisive target is efficient parallel prediction (NC), which takes precedence over general dynamical-system terminology.

sentences: A stable rectangular array contains at most three grains at each cell and is surrounded by an infinite empty lattice.
Adding one grain triggers simultaneous topplings, each sending one grain in each of the four cardinal directions.
The question asks whether a specified cell ever topples, without giving a time bound in the input.
The desired computation uses one uniform family of polynomial-size, polylogarithmic-depth Boolean circuits on the full explicit input.
Known results for other dimensions, weighted grids, boundary sinks or alternating update schemes do not settle this precisely specified planar question.

checked_sources: Read Concha-Vega–Perrot arXiv:2506.21084v1 Section 2 pages 2–4 in full: finite stable configuration on Z^2, one grain at p, existential time, and parallel threshold formula. The supplied rectangle includes p and q and explicitly stores every entry.

Read Moore–Nilsson preprint introduction, Section 3 model and dimension-dependent statements, and Section 6 discussion. It uses a finite lattice with sinks; did not silently identify that convention with the infinite-lattice formal target.

Read Concha-Vega–Loubiere–Perrot arXiv:2606.26943v1 abstract, introduction and Section 2.1 pages 1–3. Their finite-grid boundary sends grains to a sink. Used the open-status discussion with this model distinction explicitly recorded.
Checked arXiv:2602.19477v3 primary abstract and revision history, 4 March 2026: fungal H/V update sequences are a distinct process. No full proof verification of these variant results is claimed.

Bounded later searches through 2026-09-16 found no NC algorithm or unconditional nonmembership proof matching the ordinary four-neighbor, explicit-array, single-grain eventual-prediction language. Logspace-uniform NC is fixed exactly; P-completeness alone is not treated as its unconditional negation.
